To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

We see that the right-hand side is $12{e}^{2x}-{e}^{-x},$ and ${e}^{2x}$ is a term in the complementary solution, while ${e}^{-x}$ is not, so we assume that a particular solution takes the form 

$$

\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & =(\alpha x{e}^{2x}+\beta {e}^{-x})^{′} \\  & =\alpha (x{e}^{2x})^{′}+\beta ({e}^{-x})^{′} \\  & =\alpha ({e}^{2x}+2x{e}^{2x})-\beta {e}^{-x} \\  & =\alpha (1+2x){e}^{2x}-\beta {e}^{-x}\end{aligned}
